name: get_fire_detections
title: Get FIRMS fire detections
description:
Active fire / thermal anomaly detections from NASA FIRMS for an area and 1-5 UTC days, retrieved live from the FIRMS area API with the user's own FIRMS MAP_KEY.

Area: a box {west, south, east, north} in decimal degrees — longitudes first (Boise, Idaho is roughly west -116.4, south 43.4, east -116.0, north 43.8) — or 'world'. Boxes must not cross the antimeridian (split them). Days: `day_range` 1-5; without `date` you get the most recent days (today back to today-(day_range-1), UTC); with `date` you get that day and the following days. Sources: FIRMS source IDs from get_fire_data_sources; by default the three VIIRS near-real-time sources and MODIS near-real-time.

The result has a summary per source (detections, overpasses, first and last time, day/night, confidence classes, processing level, FRP statistics, extent), then a page of records (`limit`, default 50, maximum 500; 0 returns summaries only; `fields` trims each record; pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page — never construct or edit a cursor). Every result also carries `caveats` (FIRMS documentation IDs to read with get_knowledge_entry), the FIRMS Fire Map `disclaimer` and the FIRMS `citation` verbatim, a `map_link` that opens the same view in the FIRMS Fire Map, and the FIRMS request with the key redacted.

When you present results: say which satellites and UTC time window they cover; never add counts across sources or overpasses as a number of fires; describe each detection as a pixel center, not a fire's exact location or size; mention the caveats that apply; include the disclaimer's warning and the map link. `min_confidence` filters only when you ask and reports what it removed. No detections does not mean no fire (clouds, timing, latency).

Requires the user's FIRMS MAP_KEY to be connected; the key never appears in arguments or results. If the result says auth_required, ask the user to connect their key through their client — never ask them to paste it into the conversation.

recent.description: Last 24 hours (today, UTC) around Boise with the default sources
